data.description:
Evidence (tick log apps/chat/data/logs/tick-2026-08-30T19-14-54.450Z.log): project-scope .claude/settings.json permission allowlists are INERT for headless `claude -p` children. The 19:14:54Z tick tested four commands the committed allowlist (65d567e, file mtime 19:13:56Z — on disk before spawn) explicitly allows: `lattice list` [Bash(lattice *)], `node -e` [Bash(node *)], `rtk --version` [Bash(rtk *)], `git add --dry-run` [Bash(git *)] — all four denied. The log's header line gives the mechanism: 'Ignoring 9 permissions.allow entries from .claude/settings.json: this workspace has not been trusted' — a headless child never sees the trust dialog, so project-scope allow rules never load. Read-only commands that still work pass via the built-in read-only heuristic, not our rules. This disproves rung 1 of the permission ladder in apps/chat/watch/README.md:94.

FIX (board + orchestrator selected the tick's proposed fix #2): tickArgv() in apps/chat/watch/advance-watcher.mjs gains --allowedTools carrying exactly the grants from .claude/settings.json's allow list, and --disallowedTools carrying its deny list. The three force-push deny rules MUST survive — that is the git-methodology rule (force-push is always needs_human) riding on this change.

OPEN DESIGN QUESTION for the planner, decide and record why: (a) read .claude/settings.json at fire time — single source of truth, no drift; or (b) hardcode the list in tickArgv with a comment pointing at settings.json — simpler, but two places to update. CTO's read going in: fire-time read is ~6 lines with node's JSON parsing and eliminates drift, which is the exact failure class that caused this bug (settings said allowed, runtime said denied).

Verified flag syntax (claude --help, 2026-08-30): --allowedTools / --disallowedTools are variadic, 'comma or space-separated list' — the watcher spawns without a shell, so each rule rides as its own argv element.

Test impact: apps/chat/test/watcher.test.js:332 pins the exact tickArgv argv array and must account for dynamically-loaded rules; test any settings loader against a fixture settings file, not the live repo file.
data.title: advance-watcher: pass permission grants via --allowedTools/--disallowedTools in tickArgv() — project settings allowlist is inert for headless ticks

data.body: Plan committed (23d4865, branch feat/AS-21-tickargv-permission-grants). Design decision: fire-time read of .claude/settings.json via a new exported loadPermissionRules() — single source of truth; hardcoding rejected because settings-vs-runtime drift is the exact failure class that caused this bug, and same-parse sourcing makes force-push deny survival structural rather than conventional. tickArgv stays pure (rules injected as a third param), so the watcher.test.js:332 argv pin keeps asserting exact arrays via injected rules + a fixture-file loader test — never the live settings file. On unreadable settings: WARN + fire with no grant flags (today's degraded behavior); allows-without-denies is impossible by construction. Ready for developer pickup.

Implementation complete. loadPermissionRules(settingsPath) added as a separate effectful export (fire-time readFileSync+JSON.parse; missing/unreadable/malformed/non-object -> null, caller WARNs and fires without grants — no hardcoded fallback list anywhere in the watcher). tickArgv gains third param rules={allow:[],deny:[]} (zero/two-arg calls byte-identical, existing pin unchanged); appends --allowedTools then --disallowedTools iff non-empty, each rule its own argv element, deny group terminates the array. fire() wires loadPermissionRules(paths.settings) in and passes rules ?? undefined. Tests: 5 new (rules-injected exact-array pins incl. allow-only/deny-only/both-empty; loader fixtures: valid/missing/malformed/non-object/permissions-absent/non-strings-filtered; composition pin: force-push denies trail argv whenever allows present). Suite 98/98 in-container (was 93). README.md permission ladder rung 1 marked disproven with pointer to the 19:14:54Z tick log. No deviations from plan. Live verification (crit. 6) remains post-merge.

REVIEW (cold: plan + diff master...feat/AS-21-tickargv-permission-grants + in-container suite). VERDICT: PASS — 6/6 criteria. (1) Live-settings argv: loadPermissionRules on the repo's .claude/settings.json fed through tickArgv -> 20-element argv: 6 base + --allowedTools + 9 allows + --disallowedTools + 3 denies, each rule one element, deny group terminal (verified by script, not just their tests). (2) Force-push deny survival: structural (same parse, same return object) AND pinned by the composition test; deny-only input emits no bare --allowedTools. (3) Null path: loader null -> 'rules ?? undefined' -> default param -> argv byte-identical to AS-20 six-element pin; WARN logged in fire(); grep confirms zero hardcoded rule strings in the watcher (one comment mention only). (4) Back-compat: zero/two-arg tickArgv unchanged, AS-20 pin test untouched and green. (5) Suite 98/98 in-container (docker compose run test, BuildKit forced per compose.yaml header) — matches implementer's claim; all new tests use injected rules or mkdtemp fixtures, no live-settings reads. (6) Live tick verification correctly deferred post-merge per plan. ATTACKS (all held): malformed shapes null-not-throw (BOM, top-level array/number/bool, permissions-as-array, object-as-array allow, allow:'string', nested nonsense, directory path EISDIR); 5MB/50k-rule file parses; hostile rule strings (quotes, semicolons, subshell text, embedded newline) ride as ONE argv element each — no shell, no splitting. Drift check: repoRoot derives from import.meta.url (not cwd), so paths.settings hits the repo's .claude/settings.json wherever the watcher runs; fire-time read confirmed inside fire(). Commit hygiene: branch commits touch only watcher/tests/README/.lattice; CLAUDE.md blocker note remains uncommitted working-tree metawork — NOT in the branch. NON-BLOCKING observations (none violates a criterion): (a) tickArgv throws TypeError on a partial rules object ({allow} w/o deny) — unreachable via loader/default; (b) an empty-string rule in settings would ride as an empty argv element; (c) a rule whose text equals a flag name is passed as data by us but could confuse the CLI's variadic parse — requires repo write access, out of threat model; (d) top-level-array JSON yields empty lists (no WARN) rather than null — argv identical either way. No inline fixes made. Recommendation: move to done, merge --no-ff, then run criterion 6's live regression check (the four 19:14:54Z denied commands) on the next watcher-fired tick.
